Missouri.focus: ToRCH Care: regional hubs, alternative payment, digital backbone, workforce
Missouri.description: Missouri's Department of Social Services plans ToRCH Care, building on its Transformation of Rural Community Health program to create a connected system of local community hubs.
initiatives: Regional Coordinating Networks and Hub Activation
Local community hubs coordinating physical health, behavioral health and social services.
Payment models that reward collaboration leading to high-quality, high-value outcomes.
Programs to build the rural health workforce.

Montana.focus: Workforce, facility sustainability, care models, prevention and technology
Montana.description: Montana's Department of Public Health and Human Services plans five initiatives, including restructuring and partnerships to keep rural health facilities viable.
initiatives: Partnerships and restructuring to preserve access at rural health facilities.
New delivery and payment models to improve access and outcomes.
Community health and preventive infrastructure, and modern health care technologies.

Nebraska.focus: Seven initiatives: food as medicine, regionalized access, workforce and technology
Nebraska.description: Nebraska, where nearly 95% of counties are rural or frontier and 48 of 93 qualify as food deserts, plans seven initiatives for a prevention-first, tech-enabled rural health system.
initiatives: Transforming rural school kitchens, regional food hubs with farmers and ranchers, and nutrition and fitness programs.
Hub-and-spoke networks for emergency response, maternal care, post-acute follow-up and preventive care.
Recruiting and training to close care gaps.

Nevada.focus: Outcomes accelerator, provider flex fund, workforce and access
Nevada.description: Nevada plans four strategic initiatives to build reliable, sustainable care across its sparsely populated rural counties. Dollar amounts below are as proposed in the state's application.
initiatives: About $30 million proposed for value-based care and innovative chronic-disease care models.
About $40 million proposed for medical technology, equipment, mobile units and regional purchasing.
About $80 million proposed for incentives to live and serve in rural areas and tuition assistance.

New Hampshire.focus: Healthier communities, sustainable access, workforce, care models and technology
New Hampshire.description: New Hampshire's Department of Health and Human Services plans for rural communities with high-quality, affordable care close to home, supported by resilient local hospitals, a stable workforce and value-based payment.
initiatives: Disease prevention, chronic disease management, behavioral health and perinatal care.
Partnerships letting rural facilities coordinate with primary care, specialty care and EMS and share resources.
Recruitment, training and retention, and new entrants to the healthcare workforce.
Innovative technologies for efficiency, data security and digital access.
